title: Stratified keyspace mixer and KV-coverage reporter (epochal traffic runner)
author: Asha Raman
description:
Motivation: We need a workload generator that can reproduce complex keyspace skew patterns observed in production: interleaved tenant hotspots, time-varying working sets, and KV-cache sparsity transitions. Existing mix runners sample by sequence length or simple percentile weights but do not provide coordinated stratification across key dimensions (tenant, route, prefix). This PR adds a Stratified Keyspace Mixer (SKM) runner and an accompanying KV-Coverage Reporter that measures effective cache coverage and the resulting token-level cost/latency delta across epochs.

What this change introduces: 1) skm_runner: an epochal traffic generator that accepts a stratification schema (tenant buckets, prefix shards, cold/hot cohorts) and emits request traces compatible with the benchmark-lab runner interface. 2) kv_coverage_reporter: post-run analyzer that computes per-bucket cache hit estimates (prefix+kv-key level), cold-start contribution, and differential p95/p99 delta against a baseline run. 3) sample primer and deterministic seeding so runs are reproducible across CI and local envs. 4) Small harness for staged noise injection (temporal jitter, burst spikes) to exercise batching and scheduling heuristics.

Checklist: - [x] Implement core SKM runner and config parser - [x] Add single-node microbench that validates reproducibility - [x] Integrate reporter into the existing report pipeline - [x] Add docs/quickstart YAML + example workload - [x] Add unit tests for stratification sampler - [x] Run full suite in perf-candidate CI and compare to baseline.

Design notes: - The stratification schema is a compact YAML structure that maps "tenant" -> {weight, shards, hot_ratio} and an optional prefix_transformer to control synthetic key prefixes that influence KV cache locality. - SKM produces sequences annotated with `tenant_id`, `prefix_id`, and `shard_id` so the runtime's KV instrumentation can correlate observed hits. - Epoch boundaries are explicit: each epoch can change the hot_ratio or promote a cold cohort to hot to simulate cache churn. - The reporter uses conservative heuristics to estimate KV hits from observed token outputs and request hashes; it also optionally accepts ground-truth cache logs when available to compute precise coverage.

CI and performance notes: The PR triggered flaky rounds in the GPU integration test due to timing sensitivity in the burst injector; added a small backoff and stabilization sleep. CI summary: initial run had one flaky gpu-smoke failure, rerun passed all perf and unit checks.

Files of interest and how to run: - examples/stratified/README.md documents the YAML schema and quickstart - examples/stratified/tenant_mix.yaml is an opinionated baseline used in our perf deck - bench/runners/skm_runner.py is the runner implementation - bench/reporters/kv_coverage_reporter.py is the post-processor - tests/bench/test_skm_sampler.py covers deterministic seeding.

Why it matters: This runner surface lets us model real multi-tenant effects that drive tail latency and cache inefficiency; it is already useful for validating caching heuristics, scheduling improvements, and quantization tradeoffs across workloads.

Related: Linear ENG-5123 (kv-cache telemetry improvements), ENG-4981 (batcher scheduling experiments).
